text:
**Short answer:** For most weekend campers, the **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** is the best pick. It has 288Wh of LiFePO4 capacity, weighs about 8.3 lb, and costs about $249 ([PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)). One caveat: Jackery's own U.S. site no longer lists it. It has been replaced by the Explorer 300 v2, which charges faster but has a shorter warranty. The Plus is still sold through Amazon and other retailers.

**Picks by need**

| Need | Pick | Key specs | Approx. price | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Light, simple weekend trips | Jackery Explorer 300 Plus | 288Wh, 300W, ~8.3 lb | ~$249 | [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/) |
| Best value, more output | EcoFlow River 3 Plus | 286Wh, 600W, ~9.9 lb, expandable | ~$269–299 | [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/) |
| Long trips, built-in lantern | Anker SOLIX C300 | 288Wh, 300W, 5-year warranty | ~$199 | [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/) |
| Budget | Bluetti EB3A | 268Wh, 600W, ~10.1 lb | ~$179 | [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/) |
| Multi-day off-grid, space heater or e-bike not needed | Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 | 2,042Wh (1,710Wh measured), 2,200W, 39 lb | List $1,499; recently under $900 on Amazon | [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station) |
| Best value for bigger trips | Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2 | 890Wh measured, 1,800W, 25 lb | Under $530 on sale | [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station) |
| Rugged, IP65-rated, car-to-campsite | Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra | 1,536Wh, 1,800W, ~40 lb | $1,079 at Amazon | [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/) |

Prices change often, so check the current price before you buy.

**Choosing a size**
- **Phones, lights, camera batteries, a CPAP:** A 250–500Wh unit is enough. Turn the CPAP humidifier off, since it can roughly triple the machine's draw. A 288Wh unit can then run most CPAPs for 3–5 nights.
- **Fridge, fan, or several days of charging:** Step up to about 1,000Wh or more. The Explorer 2000 v2 can't run a space heater or multi-day electric cooking for long, so check your loads.
- **Weight:** Units over about 25 lb are hard to carry to a site alone.
